findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

Recovery releases every follow-up consumed by the failed run, even when the runner received it and replied before crashing. The delivered-output check protects only the turn's initial input, so the next turn can receive an answered follow-up again. Release only follow-ups that were not confirmed as handled.
findings.title: Not done: No message is lost or given twice

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

On an ordinary exhausted final retry, acknowledgeFailedTurn is true even if no reply or failure notice was delivered. handleFailure then preserves the consumed input, leaving the unanswered message unavailable to the next turn.
findings.title: Not done: No message is lost or given twice

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

The migration looks up a marker only by the work item's exact queue_jid. Existing marker recovery also supports older base conversation and thread keys (runtime-app.ts:404–418), while admission items use agent- and provider-qualified queue keys (canonical-message-repository.postgres.ts:377–382). An already-read item whose saved marker is under a base key remains unconsumed and replays after the switch. The backfill test seeds only an exact queue key.
findings.title: Not done: backfill from the saved marker

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

The spawned child workers take repository input and fetch messages, then exit without admitting a turn, delivering a continuation, or sending a reply. The active-turn follow-up test constructs both workers in one process with callback runners. These tests cannot detect loss or duplication during the required cross-process handoff through reply.
findings.title: Not done: two-process no-loss/no-duplication test

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

The supplied Functional check describes existing Postgres scenarios for callable completion and a missing-runner follow-up, while saying Postgres will be rerun later. It does not describe exercising the covered two-worker, settings-reload, restart, and before/after-output failure paths as a user would, so it skips material parts of this story.
findings.title: Not done: functional check

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

takeInput selects by receiveOrder, but this presentation sort gives provider timestamps precedence. A delayed attachment or a provider timestamp that moves backward can place a later-received message before an earlier one in the agent's batch. Use receiveOrder when it is available.
findings.title: Present taken messages in receive order

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

This added file records a prior review result and task status. It is outside the permitted paths and is unnecessary for the runtime switch, migration, tests, or decision update.
findings.title: Remove the review-state file outside the allowed scope

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

A final retry with a generic runner error and no delivered reply sets `acknowledgeFailedTurn` and returns here without calling `releaseInput`. Those work items remain consumed, so a later turn cannot take the unanswered messages. The new unit test explicitly expects this preservation, leaving the required before-reply recovery untested.
findings.title: Not done: No message is lost or given twice

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

The new subprocess test runs only `takeInput` and `getMessagesByIds`; it never starts admission, a live turn, or a reply in either process. The follow-up scenario below uses two worker objects in one process. Together they do not test the required two-process delivery path for dropped or doubled messages through the real entry point.
findings.title: Not done: two-process end-to-end no-loss test

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

The supplied functional check cites existing Postgres scenarios for callable completion and a missing runner, then says Postgres will be rerun. It does not describe exercising the covered two-worker, settings-reload, restart, or before- and after-reply failure flows as a user would. The check therefore skips material parts of this change's required behavior.
findings.title: Not done: functional check

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

`takeInput` returns work items in database receive order, but this sort gives provider timestamps precedence. A delayed media message or a provider timestamp that runs behind the local clock can therefore be shown to the agent before an earlier received message. The added unit test even expects this reordering. Preserve `receiveOrder` when presenting the batch.
findings.title: Present the batch in receive order
